rationale: The candidate is a coherent compact object in all four views, but it reads as a chunky stepped prism with limited public-space generosity. The mass responds only weakly to the access edge: the blue frontage is not met by a clearly opened court, seam, or undercut, so the street threshold remains semantically sealed. The top view suggests a parcel-aware orientation, yet the dominant gesture is still mostly box-like with a clipped upper form rather than a clear neighborhood-building figure. The silhouette has some section interest, but the stepping feels more like a generic tiered compression than a program-driven terrace or inhabited roof. Overall it is repairable and not visibly self-colliding, but the visible mass does not yet support the neighborhood_living brief strongly enough to pass program fit.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More civic pavilion/community-center than neighborhood living; softer public enclosure than active ground-edge housing/commercial logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Curved parapet massing with a large central void and bridge-like connection can support a neighborhood/public interior threshold.
